---
title: "tribble() accepts a column of functions that tibble() rejects"
ref: TDY-12
categories: [tidyverse]
impact: incoherent
attendu: "the same table, or the same error, with both constructors"
versions: "All versions of {tibble}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2021)"
---

::: {.piege packages="tibble"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tibble))

tibble(name = "mean", f = mean)
tribble(
  ~name,  ~f,
  "mean", mean
)
```
:::

## Why

A tibble column must be a vector, and a function is not one: `tibble()` rejects it. `tribble()` reads its values cell by cell and, when a cell is not a simple value, it stores the column in a list. The function then becomes an element of a list-column, which is allowed.

## The remedy

Build the list-column explicitly with `list()`, which works everywhere, then call the function with `[[ ]]`.

::: {.piege packages="tibble"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tibble))

tools <- tibble(name = c("mean", "median"), f = list(mean, median))
tools
tools$f[[2]](c(1, 2, 10))
```
:::
